Kiernozia Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kiernozia, Poland

Demolished. Kiernozia's first Jewish settlers arrived at the start of the 19th century, forming an independent kehilla by 1830 and reaching about 300 people (40 percent of the town) in the interwar period, most working in small trade and crafts. In March 1940, the Germans established a ghetto here holding about 650 Jews from Kiernozia and surrounding towns, liquidated in March 1941 with all residents deported to the Warsaw Ghetto. This cemetery, likely established in the second half of the 19th century, saw its last burials between 1939 and 1945. Around 1946, Holocaust survivor Jan Geiss erected a monument here in honor of Kiernozia's Jews and fenced part of the site.
